A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same paper, Extreme Rotation Estimation in the Wild, with complete supplementary Sections 7–10. Text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ELP and StreetLearn evaluations, qualitative results and ablations in the main paper and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains original evaluations and reports additional homography comparisons, component ablations, baseline finetuning and cross-scene experiments.

M1.justification: The LoFTR feature extractor, auxiliary channels, rotation transformer, three 360-bin Euler-angle heads and progressive learning pipeline are retained. The new token-initialization subsection explains an existing component rather than introducing a new method.

E1.justification: v3 adds a test of 200 image pairs sampled from different scenes, examining inputs without a shared location (Section 9, Figure 10). Existing training sources and StreetLearn, sELP and wELP benchmark coverage remain.

E2.justification: The six main baseline families are retained. v3 adds homography-based SIFT and LoFTR comparisons, including on StreetLearn (Table 7), and an augmentation-finetuned DenseCorrVol comparison (Table 13).

E3.justification: Table 1 revises ELP training from 89,149 pairs across 6,398 scenes to 76,595 pairs across 5,883 scenes and adds validation partitions. Section 8.4 reports balanced-validation monitoring with stopping when MGE improvement falls below 0.5 degrees. Added experiments introduce homography estimation and baseline-finetuning protocols. The balanced-validation total is internally inconsistent, leaving its exact size uncertain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v3 adds joint removal of InstructPix2Pix and SegFormer (Table 10), augmentation finetuning of DenseCorrVol (Table 13), homography-versus-essential-matrix comparisons (Table 7), and a cross-scene input check (Figure 10). These substantially expand tests of component dependence, comparison settings and unusual inputs.

E5.justification: The reported SIFT/LoFTR seed of 12345 is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added cross-scene histogram describes outputs across inputs rather than uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: v3 replaces numerous ELP and ablation entries and adds results in Tables 7, 10 and 13 and Figure 10. For example, Table 2 non-overlap MGE changes from 13.36 to 13.62 degrees on sELP and from 27.49 to 26.97 degrees on wELP. These updates accompany revised training/validation settings and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Euler decomposition, overlap conditions, geodesic-error definition, graph-based selection rule and augmentation-filter mathematics are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the ELP benchmark, a transformer-based rotation estimator and progressive training for real-world extreme views. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 explains why large FoV disparities can pair architectural details with broader scene views. It also interprets the new prior-removal and baseline-finetuning experiments as evidence about the sources of the method's advantage. Existing applicability boundaries and yaw-ambiguity explanations remain.

D1.justification: New Section 8.2 documents standard-normal initialization of learnable Euler-angle tokens and loading their optimized weights at inference. v3 also specifies validation-based stopping. Most architecture dimensions, optimizer settings, hardware, training times and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to photo-to-terrain alignment, RelocNet, CamNet and LRM, and connects its learnable tokens to LRM/PF-LRM. The broader positioning relative to matching-based methods and previous extreme-rotation estimators remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized additions explain FoV filtering, validation, token initialization and new experiments, alongside wording corrections and subsection renumbering. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds supplementary Tables 7, 10 and 13 and Figure 10, expands Table 1 with validation rows, and adds metric-direction arrows. Existing figures and tables are retained with localized reflow, including Figure 5 moving from PDF page 6 to page 7; the visual design remains consistent.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, explicit validation/stopping documentation and targeted component and baseline controls improve transparency and better probe explanations for performance. The gains are limited by new reporting errors: Table 1's balanced-validation categories sum to 854 but its total says 8,238, and the homography discussion attributes LoFTR's approximately 2.1-to-2.5-degree change to SIFT. These issues temper the useful additions.
